claude.performance_metric: cost estimate rose $52B to $54B; start-up slipped from late-2014/Q1-2015 to mid-2015; no divestiture or impairment; 47.3% operated interest retained
claude.rationale: The slice documents only a modest cost-estimate increase ($52B to $54B) and a schedule slip (to mid-2015), with 55% then ~75% of activities completed and 20 of 21 Train 1 modules installed — no documented disruption at the product/process interface, so p4_pathway = 0. Neither filing states any cause (labor, contractor, engineering) and no operations-versus-organization fracture is reported; ownership, operatorship, and offtake commitments remained unchanged, so p5_pathway = 0. No archetype incoherence or business-model incompatibility is documented, and no divestiture, impairment, or write-down specific to Gorgon is reported.

gemini.performance_metric: cost estimate rose from $52 billion to $54 billion
gemini.rationale: The slice documents a cost increase from $52 billion to $54 billion and a schedule slip to mid-2015. However, it explicitly states that no cause is given for these changes, and there is no documented evidence of product/process incoherence (p4) or process/organization fracture (p5).

grok.performance_metric: cost +$2B to $54B; start-up slipped to mid-2015; no divestiture
grok.rationale: The slice documents only a $2B rise in the Gorgon first-phase cost estimate ($52B to $54B) and a start-up slip from late 2014/Q1 2015 to mid-2015 across the FY2012–FY2013 10-Ks, with ownership, operatorship, and offtake commitments unchanged and no impairment or divestiture. No realized product/process interface incoherence (p4) is stated; the filings give no cause for the cost/schedule change and do not describe any inability to align product with operating processes. No process/organization fracture (p5) is documented; nothing in the window filings addresses operations-versus-people/management/culture breakdown over time.
